This reference architecture defines the draft AWS API Management blueprint — pending Domain EA and Security Architecture review — for enterprise API exposure, consumption, and governance using managed AWS services and enterprise controls already defined in existing standards and security guidance.

page_texts.6:
[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#scope-and-applicability]

### Scope and Applicability

This architecture applies to teams implementing API Management capabilities on AWS for internal, partner, or external APIs where lifecycle management, centralized policy enforcement, and operational visibility are required.

> **Scope: Amazon API Gateway REST APIs.** This reference architecture's topologies and controls — including the Private (`PRIVATE`) endpoint type for the mandatory East-West control-plane baseline, direct AWS WAF Web ACL association to the gateway stage, and (where referenced) usage plans and request validators — are scoped to Amazon API Gateway **REST APIs**. HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs do not support the same endpoint-type set (no Private/PrivateLink endpoint type, no Edge-optimized endpoint type — Regional is the only option for both), do not support direct WAF Web ACL association to the API resource in the same way REST API stages do, and do not support usage plans or REST-style request validators. A domain team implementing an API as an HTTP API or WebSocket API must not assume this reference architecture's Private-endpoint or WAF-association topology applies unmodified. For the Private-endpoint control specifically, a VPC Link/NLB integration is **not** an equivalent — VPC Link only privatizes the API Gateway-to-backend integration, it does not make the HTTP or WebSocket API's own client-facing endpoint non-internet-routable. Per [STD-APP-API-007](../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md) Requirement 5 (the authoritative source for this framing), the cited AWS security SBB's control — API Gateway interception plus private, non-internet-routable gateway endpoints — applies to REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs alike, with no exception by API type; HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs, however, do not support a Private endpoint type, so there is no technical mechanism by which they can satisfy that control today. This is a genuine, unresolved SBB/technical-capability gap — it is not something this reference architecture (or an implementing team) can resolve on its own authority. The only currently sanctioned path is to implement that East-West boundary as a REST API using the Private (`PRIVATE`) endpoint type; any HTTP or WebSocket API East-West boundary that cannot be re-platformed as REST is an open compliance gap that must be tracked and remediated through Security Architecture's SBB exception process (or an SBB amendment) — no internal Application Load Balancer, other private frontend, or VPC Link/NLB integration is authorized as a sanctioned substitute for the SBB's control until that process resolves the gap. For the WAF-association control, CloudFront- or ALB-fronted WAF association remain applicable equivalents for that API type. Coordinate with Platform Engineering and Security Architecture on the applicable control before proceeding. This scope is consistent with [GUID-APP-IMPL-011](../../guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-011-aws-api-management-platform-guidance.md), which is likewise scoped to REST APIs for its endpoint-visibility guidance.

[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#logical-request-and-control-flow-view]

### Logical Request and Control-Flow View

The diagram below shows the North-South (external consumer) and East-West (internal service-to-service) request paths through the Private API Gateway, WAF, Authorizer, and backend services described throughout this reference architecture.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph NorthSouth["North-South (external)"]
        Consumer[External / Partner Consumer] --> WAF[AWS WAF]
        WAF --> RegionalGW[Amazon API Gateway - Regional Endpoint]
    end

    subgraph EastWest["East-West (internal)"]
        InternalConsumer[Upstream Internal Service] --> PrivateGW[Amazon API Gateway - Private Endpoint]
    end

    RegionalGW --> Authorizer[Lambda Authorizer - Entra ID / GPD JWT Validation]
    PrivateGW --> Authorizer
    Authorizer -->|Deny policy| Reject[401 / 403 Response]
    Authorizer -->|Allow policy returned to gateway| GatewayIntegration[API Gateway Integration - performs backend invocation]
    GatewayIntegration -->|Kubernetes/EKS| Mesh[Service Mesh Sidecar - Istio or Linkerd, mTLS + Traffic Policy]
    Mesh --> BackendEKS[Backend Services - EKS]
    GatewayIntegration -->|Lambda/ECS| BackendServerless[Backend Services - Lambda / ECS]
    BackendEKS --> OTel[OTel SDK + Collector]
    OTel --> Dynatrace[Dynatrace - Primary APM]
    BackendServerless --> CWXRay[CloudWatch / X-Ray]
    RegionalGW --> GWLogs[Gateway Access Logs]
    PrivateGW --> GWLogs
    GWLogs --> CWLogs[Amazon CloudWatch Logs]
    CWLogs --> SIEM[Enterprise SIEM]
    RegionalGW -.->|management-plane API calls, independent of the request path| CloudTrail[AWS CloudTrail]
    PrivateGW -.->|management-plane API calls, independent of the request path| CloudTrail
```

> **Authorizer scope note:** The Lambda authorizer only returns an allow/deny policy to API Gateway — it never invokes a backend directly. On Allow, API Gateway itself (the Gateway Integration step above) performs the backend invocation; on Deny, API Gateway returns the 401/403 response without ever reaching a backend.
page_texts.26:
[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#deployment-and-trust-boundary-view]

### Deployment and Trust-Boundary View

The diagram below shows the VPC/subnet/endpoint trust boundaries and where the Private API Gateway, service mesh, and backend compute sit relative to those boundaries.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Internet["Public Internet"]
        ExtConsumer[External / Partner Consumer]
    end

    subgraph AWSRegional["AWS-Managed Regional Services (outside any customer VPC)"]
        WAF2[AWS WAF Web ACL]
        RegionalGW2[Amazon API Gateway - Regional Endpoint]
        PrivateGW2[Amazon API Gateway - Private Endpoint - regional service, reachable only via VPC Interface Endpoint]
        Lambda[Lambda Functions - AWS-managed execution environment, not customer-VPC-resident]
        WAF2 --> RegionalGW2
    end

    subgraph AWSAccount["AWS Account / VPC"]
        subgraph PrivateSubnet["Private Subnet(s)"]
            VPCEndpoint[VPC Interface Endpoint - execute-api, Private Endpoint Policy]
            VPCLink[VPC Link]
            NLBTarget[NLB / ALB - VPC Link private integration target, per active SBB]
            LambdaENI[Lambda Hyperplane ENI - optional VPC attachment, network access only]

            subgraph ComputeBoundary["Backend Compute Trust Boundary"]
                ECS[ECS Services]
                subgraph EKSCluster["EKS Cluster"]
                    MeshSidecars[Service Mesh - Istio or Linkerd Sidecars, mTLS]
                    EKSServices[EKS-Deployed Application Services]
                    MeshSidecars --> EKSServices
                end
            end
        end
    end

    ExtConsumer -->|HTTPS| WAF2
    RegionalGW2 -->|Native Lambda integration, no VPC Link| Lambda
    RegionalGW2 -->|VPC Link, HTTPS only| VPCLink
    VPCLink --> NLBTarget
    NLBTarget --> ECS
    NLBTarget --> MeshSidecars

    VPCEndpoint -->|AWS PrivateLink| PrivateGW2
    PrivateGW2 -->|Internal callers only, no internet route; native Lambda integration| Lambda
    PrivateGW2 -->|VPC Link, HTTPS only| VPCLink
    Lambda -.->|optional: Hyperplane ENI for network access into selected subnets; execution environment remains AWS-managed| LambdaENI
```

> **Integration-path note:** API Gateway invokes Lambda through native Lambda/AWS integration — never through VPC Link. VPC Link private integrations (used for the ECS and EKS/mesh container paths on both the Regional and Private gateways) terminate at an NLB/ALB target per the active SBB's `VPC Link + NLB + Target Group` pattern; the active SBB's control mapping names only NLB/ALB targets, not Cloud Map, so Cloud Map is not depicted as a VPC Link target here. Neither gateway invokes ECS or the mesh sidecars directly.
>
> **Lambda placement note:** Lambda Functions are shown among AWS-Managed Regional Services, outside the customer VPC/private-subnet boundary. Lambda's execution environment is an AWS-managed regional service; it is never customer-VPC-resident regardless of configuration. When a Lambda function is configured with VPC access, AWS provisions Hyperplane ENIs in the selected private subnets solely to give that execution environment network reachability into the VPC (e.g., to call VPC-internal backends) — this optional attachment provides network access only and does not relocate the Lambda execution environment itself into the VPC. The diagram depicts this optional attachment as a separate `LambdaENI` node rather than placing the `Lambda` node inside the VPC/subnet boundary.

[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#service-architecture]

#### Service Architecture

- Edge/API ingress services (North-South): API Gateway fronts all external-facing and partner-facing APIs.
- Internal service APIs (East-West): [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) mandates a Private API Gateway (**REST API**, endpoint type `PRIVATE`, VPC Endpoint-only — see Scope and Applicability for why this reference architecture's Private-endpoint topology is REST-API-scoped) as the control-plane baseline for internal service-to-service traffic (REQ-APIGW-01/03/04; Pattern B: Internal East-West). Service mesh (mTLS, circuit breaking, traffic policies) MAY be layered on top of the Private API Gateway baseline for fine-grained service identity and traffic management — it complements, and does not replace, gateway interception. See [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md) for the service mesh pattern and [STD-APP-API-006](../../../standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) for the gateway-vs-mesh decision guidance.
- Shared platform services for security and telemetry

[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#technology-stack]

#### Technology Stack

| Layer | Technologies | Rationale | Alternatives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Edge/API | Amazon API Gateway | Managed API ingress and policy controls for North-South APIs | NGINX/Kong/self-managed gateways |
| Identity | Entra ID (Gainwell GPD), IAM, external OIDC/SAML IdP | Federated identity and token-based access | External IdP-only models |
| Protection | AWS WAF, AWS Shield | Layer-7 and DDoS protection controls | Third-party WAF appliances |
| Application Instrumentation | OpenTelemetry SDK + OTel Collector | Vendor-neutral application-level traces, metrics, and logs per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) — proposed for Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services, pending that standard's ratification (currently `status: draft`); Collector routes to Dynatrace (primary enterprise APM) | For Kubernetes/EKS-deployed services, no conformant alternative once ratified — vendor SDKs are only permitted as OTel exporters |
| Observability Backends | Amazon CloudWatch, AWS X-Ray, AWS CloudTrail | AWS-native compute resource metrics/logs (Lambda, ECS) and management-plane telemetry; supplements, does not replace, Dynatrace as the primary APM for OTel-routed application telemetry | Required baseline for Lambda/ECS backends outside Kubernetes/EKS scope |
| Integration | Lambda, ECS/EKS, private integration via VPC Link | Flexible backend integration | Direct internet backends (not preferred) |
| Internal Service Communication | Private API Gateway (mandatory baseline on AWS) + Service Mesh (Istio or Linkerd, per the active [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md) pattern; [STD-INFRA-EKS-001](../../../standards/infrastructure/eks/STD-INFRA-EKS-001-eks-auto-mode-container-compute.md) REQ-EKS-007b proposes narrowing the approved set to Istio only, pending that standard's ratification — currently `status: draft`) | Private API Gateway satisfies REQ-APIGW-01/03/04; the service mesh adds mTLS, traffic policy, and observability as a complementary layer for East-West service-to-service APIs | Direct service calls with Kubernetes NetworkPolicy (mesh omitted; Private API Gateway remains mandatory) |

[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#component-1-api-gateway-runtime]

#### Component 1: API Gateway Runtime

**Purpose:** Enforce request routing, authentication/authorization, quotas, and policy at API ingress.

**Responsibilities:**

- Route requests to approved backend services.
- Enforce existing gateway and API security controls.
- Emit runtime and audit telemetry.

**Technical Specifications:**

- Supports Amazon API Gateway **REST APIs** (this reference architecture's scoped API type — see Scope and Applicability). HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs are out of scope for the Private-endpoint and WAF-association topology described here; teams implementing those API types must coordinate an equivalent, separately-designed control set.
- Integrates with token validation and policy authorization.
- Supports staged deployment and versioned APIs.

[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#component-2-api-lifecycle-management-plane]

#### Component 2: API Lifecycle Management Plane

**Purpose:** Govern API publication, versioning, and promotion.

**Responsibilities:**

- Manage API definitions and stage promotion workflows.
- Integrate standards checks in CI/CD.
- Enforce release and deprecation governance.

**Technical Specifications:**

- Contract-first API definition management.
- Pipeline-based validation against standards and policies.
- Traceable promotion from non-production to production.

page_texts.76:
[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#recovery-objectives]

#### Recovery Objectives

- Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) are domain-defined per API and set at onboarding based on business criticality; no enterprise-wide RTO/RPO is mandated by this reference architecture.
- Business impact assessment determines criticality tier (e.g., PHI-bearing or revenue-critical APIs require the most aggressive RTO/RPO).
page_texts.77:
[strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md#recovery-strategies]

#### Recovery Strategies

- **Configuration recovery**: API Gateway stage configuration, WAF Web ACLs, and IAM/Entra ID integration are defined as IaC and restored by redeploying the same source-controlled templates; configuration is not a manually-recreated artifact.
- **Availability and failover**: Use multi-AZ deployment for gateway and backend compute; for multi-region availability requirements, replicate the gateway and identity integration stack to a secondary region per the domain's approved regional failover strategy.
- **Backup and restore**: Backend datastores follow their own domain-specific backup/restore procedures; this reference architecture does not introduce new data backup requirements beyond what the backend technology standard already requires.
- **Continuity responsibilities**: Platform Engineering owns recovery of shared gateway, WAF, and identity integration infrastructure; domain teams own recovery of their backend services and data stores. Both parties test their portion of the recovery plan during scheduled DR exercises.
